note: Normalized round/telemetry shape for the native tool-call + tool-result continuation case. Sanitized: no request or response bodies, no model prose, no tool arguments, no corpus/session/request ids, no endpoints, no timestamps, no token counts, no latencies. Prompt identity is expressed as `prompt_repeats_round` (a symbolic back-reference) instead of copying live token counts.
why_this_shape_matters: Distinguishes a provider fault from a host-side evidence refusal. Both cases below completed every provider round normally; they differ only in whether the host's bounded log tool yielded a citeable evidence identity.

cases.summary: Tool result carried a citeable event identity, so the host admitted it and the next round synthesized a grounded answer.

Tool result reported result_count=1 from a pattern-matched template whose events were all excluded by a structured filter, so it carried no citeable identity. The host evidence gate refused it, the model context never gained the result, so the next round re-sent the same prompt and the model repeated the same call. The host non-progress bound then withdrew the only required tool, leaving later rounds unable to satisfy the grounding instruction they were still given.
